hero.description: Xalor is an ahead-of-time (AOT) type reification engine. It acts as a hybrid bridge between your build pipeline and your live production environment by treating native TypeScript interfaces as the single source of truth.

whatIsXalor.description: Xalor shifts heavy type parsing from the browser directly to your build toolchain. It compiles your native, pristine TypeScript types into lightweight, hidden blueprints—completely **eliminating production runtime overhead** and dual-source schema maintenance code loops.
whatIsXalor.subDescription: Instead of parsing graphs or reconstructing types at runtime, Xalor executes against precompiled, content-addressed structures created entirely during the build process, yielding a flat _0.8KB client bundle footprint_.

stepOne.description: Write standard TypeScript interfaces. No DSLs or setup—your types become the source of truth.

stepTwo.description: A background compiler indexes your code and builds optimized type snapshots for instant reuse.

stepThree.description: At runtime, Xalor uses precompiled structures for fast validation and transformation with zero overhead.

header.description: Stop maintaining separate verification engines and mock data setups. Xalor converts native types into high-speed runtime systems with zero bundle inflation.

tag.subDescription: Catch structural failures instantly at your system boundaries.

util.description: Synchronously parses unknown input into a typed structure. Validates against the expected schema at runtime and either returns a fully typed instance or triggers a controlled validation failure through the auditor pipeline when constraints are violated.

tag.subDescription: Instant mockup datasets generated without maintaining fixture files.

util.description: Generates realistic mock datasets from a typed schema blueprint. Traverses the input structure to produce property-compliant values with configurable constraints for testing, prototyping, and simulation.

tag.subDescription: Peel away unsafe variables without redefining your schemas.

util.description: Performs a strongly-typed deep merge between two object graphs following a defined schema blueprint. Traverses nested structures recursively, resolving conflicts using deterministic merge rules: explicit null values override baseline fields, undefined values defer to baseline state, and array indices are merged positionally with safe out-of-bounds extension support for patch payloads.

tag.subDescription: Evaluate un-typed runtime payloads against registered type blueprints.

util.description: Distributed systems rarely deploy in perfect lockstep. drift provides a runtime compatibility bridge that safely validates legacy payloads against previous contracts and upgrades them to your latest type definitions in memory, helping services evolve independently without breaking consumers.

header.description: Answers to the most common questions about how Xalor works, why it exists, and how it approaches the gap between TypeScript types and runtime data.

faqItemsList.question: What is Xalor?
faqItemsList.description:
Xalor is an ambient type reification engine for TypeScript. It preserves the structural knowledge that TypeScript normally erases during compilation and turns it into lightweight runtime blueprints for validation, transformation, diagnostics, and future runtime capabilities.

→ Read: [What is Xalor?](/docs/xalor-overview/01_WHAT_IS_XALOR)

faqItemsList.question: Is Xalor another runtime validation library?
faqItemsList.description:
No. Validation is one application of Xalor, but the core idea is much larger. Traditional validators recreate runtime schemas manually. Xalor preserves your existing TypeScript type information and makes that knowledge available at runtime.

→ Read: [Xalor Value](/docs/xalor-overview/03_XALOR_VALUE)

faqItemsList.question: Why not just use Zod?
faqItemsList.description:
Zod provides an excellent schema-first approach to runtime validation. Xalor takes a different approach by treating native TypeScript types as the source of truth and extracting runtime knowledge automatically, eliminating the need to maintain duplicate schemas.

→ Read: [Xalor vs Traditional Approaches](/docs/xalor-overview/06_XALOR_VS_TRADITIONAL_APPROACHES)

faqItemsList.question: How is Xalor different from tools like Typia?
faqItemsList.description:
Tools like Typia generate optimized validation code from TypeScript types. Xalor focuses on creating a reusable runtime type layer, where structural information can be stored, shared, inspected, and used beyond validation alone.

→ Read: [Xalor vs Traditional Approaches](/docs/xalor-overview/06_XALOR_VS_TRADITIONAL_APPROACHES)

faqItemsList.question: Do I need to rewrite my existing TypeScript types?
faqItemsList.description:
No. Xalor is designed around standard TypeScript interfaces and types. Your existing TypeScript definitions remain the source of truth instead of requiring a new schema language or duplicate representation.

→ Read: [Why Use Xalor?](/docs/xalor-overview/05_WHY_USE_XALOR)

faqItemsList.question: Does Xalor send my TypeScript types to production?
faqItemsList.description:
No. Xalor performs extraction during build time and produces compact runtime artifacts. The compiler tooling and type interpretation logic remain outside of your production application bundle.

→ Read: [Package Build Architecture](/docs/architecture/05_PACKAGE_BUILD_ARCHITECTURE)

faqItemsList.question: When does Xalor do its work?
faqItemsList.description:
Xalor moves expensive structural analysis into the build process. Runtime execution uses precomputed blueprints instead of repeatedly interpreting schemas or rebuilding type information on demand.

→ Read: [Build Pipeline](/docs/architecture/02_BUILD_PIPELINE)

faqItemsList.question: Does Xalor require decorators or a new way of writing TypeScript?
faqItemsList.description:
No. Xalor is designed to work alongside normal TypeScript development patterns. Developers continue writing native interfaces and types while Xalor handles the runtime representation layer.

→ Read: [Getting Started](/docs/getting-started)

faqItemsList.question: What can Xalor enable beyond validation?
faqItemsList.description:
Once runtime type knowledge exists, applications can build capabilities that traditionally require manually maintained schemas, including diagnostics, data transformation, API contracts, migrations, developer tooling, and entirely new runtime APIs.

→ Read: [Xalor Value](/docs/xalor-overview/03_XALOR_VALUE)

faqItemsList.question: Who benefits most from using Xalor?
faqItemsList.description:
Xalor is designed for teams working on large TypeScript systems where maintaining schemas, contracts, validation logic, and data models becomes increasingly difficult. It is especially useful for applications with complex data boundaries and performance requirements.

→ Read: [Who Is Xalor For?](/docs/xalor-overview/04_WHO_IS_XALOR_FOR)
